text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyA Look Back at the Most Breathtaking Photos of Saturn From Voyager 1It visited the ringed planet 46 years ago this monthJCBy Jake Currie6:00 PM CST on November 9, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleVoyage 1 is holding on for dear life. The spacecraft recently went inexplicably incommunicado after a carefully planned software update rerouted power to prolong its 49-year-old mission. Thankfully, Voyager 1 seems to have restored communication just as mysteriously as it cut it off. Now it’s on the cusp of marking a milestone. On November 18th, Voyager 1 will reach one light day from Earth (the distance light travels in 24 hours).Powered By 107.1K 00ShareNextStayRead more: “Astronomers Spot a Strange Atmospheric Wave Above Saturn’s South Pole”Forty-six years ago this month (when Voyager was just a precocious toddler), it was performing a flyby of Saturn and beaming breathtaking images of the ringed planet and its many moons. We’ve collected some of the best below, but first, let’s take a look at one of the greatest close-up images of Saturn humanity had before Voyager’s trip. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
